notes.title: 🧭 Exploring environments in Flint: Treasure of Oblivion
notes.content:
In your role as a pirate captain, you can travel the world to seek out new companions and fabulous treasures in [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i]. Read on to learn more about the exploration phases in Savage Level’s tactical RPG.

[h2]“[i]Exploration is at the core of the experience[/i]”[/h2]
Built on solid turn-based combat and crew management mechanics, Flint: Treasure of Oblivion will also give players the freedom to explore. From the town and its lively streets to the pirate ship navigating stormy seas and the temple deep in the jungle, more than 20 unique locations are waiting to be discovered.

“[i]Exploration is at the core of the experience, and it helps us strengthen the narrative dimension[/i],” explained Johan Spielmann, Game Director. “Flint: Treasure of Oblivion [i]is a pirate story where the key events are told through comic panels. As they investigate the various locations, players will be able to learn more about the world through environmental narration[/i].”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/671786fe73099de7f8720d8e61f34729049f2cd4.jpg[/img]

Beyond the pleasure of voyaging and delving deeper into the story, exploring the world will offer a tactical advantage in [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i]. It brings opportunities to find and recruit powerful optional characters, or unearth weapons and treatments that can be decisive in combat. “[i]These benefits aren’t served up on a platter[/i],” added Johan. “[i]The concept is kind of like ‘Where's Waldo?’ in that we want to encourage players to understand and carefully observe the world around them in order to get rewards[/i].”

[h2]Detailed, vivid and realistic environments[/h2]
The studio Savage Level put a lot of work into the environments to make the exploration phases as enjoyable as possible. First, the locations are bustling with life, including plenty of dialogue between NPCs and random events. “[i]Without trying to make a documentary, we wanted to immerse the players in all those everyday moments[/i],” commented Johan.

The team also sought to get as close as possible to life as it was in the eighteenth century, including the architecture, apparel and customs. For instance, they consulted historical maps of Saint-Malo to faithfully recreate the French town, and studied boat designs at the National Navy Museum. “[i]The idea is to get away from the romantic depictions of Hollywood, with a more authentic approach to piracy in this period[/i],” explained Johan.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/c0722df13c27c217291b9f04a8f082ef21070c8c.jpg[/img]

Lastly, the scenery in [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i] was painstakingly created by the artists, in Unreal Engine 5, to offer recognizable visuals and masses of detail. “[i]We wanted to make sure that players will feel no inconsistency as they move from reading the comic panels to exploring the three-dimensional world[/i],” Johan told us. “[i]So each medium has a strong artistic identity, and a wealth of detail that players can get lost in[/i].”

[h2]Will you manage to discover all the hidden secrets?[/h2]
Savage Level has pulled out all the stops with the environments to immerse you in the Golden Age of Piracy like never before. “[i]We want to encourage players to be curious, to explore everything, and to find each detail in the story[/i],” summed up Johan.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/07dd6b9a97a3fc28812063259816778eff026eee.jpg[/img]

notes.title: 🎼 Diving deep into the Golden Age of Piracy through the sounds of Flint
notes.content:
With [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i], players will be able to experience an epic pirate adventure as if they were there, thanks in large part to an immersive sound environment. Here, we will explore the music and sounds designed by the studio Savage Level – grab your headphones and let’s begin!

[h2]A soundtrack with diverse inspirations[/h2]

Your adventure in the boots of Captain Flint will be driven by the music of [b]Winifred Phillips[/b], the award-winning composer behind the soundtracks of [i]Shattered State[/i] and [i]Assassin’s Creed: Liberation[/i]. “[i]We chose Winifred because she ticked all the boxes,[/i]” stated Khatchadour Babélian, Audio Director at Savage Level.

Players will hear various music in this tactical RPG: as they explore Europe, there will be folk tunes played on instruments such as the accordion, violin and piano; then, as they reach the New World, their ears will be greeted by the sounds of traditional cultures, percussion (such as the African conga and talking drum), and shamanic chants.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/99312f423456a1d28791c2f1618bc16ddaf00647.jpg[/img]
[i]Winnifred Phillips[/i]

“[i]We are principally featuring eighteenth-century instruments[/i],” commented Khatchadour. “[i]The Art Department at Savage Level did a lot of research to achieve a degree of historical authenticity. But they gave themselves the license to add a few modern touches, with a bit of electric guitar or synth here and there.[/i]”

It was important for Khatchadour that players will be able to enjoy the soundtrack throughout their adventure, without feeling like turning down the volume or turning it off altogether. So he asked Winifred to provide separate tracks, in order to create variations on each piece of music and avoid monotony. Savage Level’s art department also suggested composing fairly minimalistic pieces, to avoid things getting overloaded once the various sound effects were added.

[h2]The creative process for sounds and voices[/h2]

[i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i] is filled with sound effects, including lapping waves, screeching gulls and rowdy taverns. Khatchadour mixed various samples from his library to create custom effects. “[i]In the case of the musket, I chose one sound for the lock, one for the detonation, and yet another for the bullet impact, which produces a result that is unique to our game,[/i]” explained the Audio Director.

Going even further, Khatchadour also recorded some of the sounds from scratch, like door knocks and the whistle of a sword. He told us that “[i]these were effects that I produced myself in the studio, using objects to hand. It’s one of the most fun parts of the job![/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/836c0e7872ac265d413637fdebfe1a4a11ee88fe.jpg[/img]
[i]Khatchadour Babélian[/i]

Finally, the game includes English and French dubbing, in particular for the narrator’s voice during the cut-scenes. For these, Savage Level turned to the localization studio Native Prime, which has worked on acclaimed franchises such as [i]Hitman[/i] and [i]Professor Layton[/i]. All of the sound effects and voices were spatialized to enhance the immersive experience.

[h2]Prepare to set sail in just a few weeks![/h2]

With this collection of sound effects designed by Khatchadour and songs composed by Winifred, Savage Level is hoping to transport you into a foreign world. “[i]My aim is to take players back into this period and to allow them to experience the life of a pirate captain,[/i]” stated the Audio Director. Are you ready to begin your story?

[h3]Listen to the main theme, composed by Winifred Phillips[/h3]

notes.title: 🤝Meet Savage Level, the crew behind Flint: Treasure of Oblivion🏴‍☠️
notes.content:
On 24 October 2024, players will be able to jump on board [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i], an epic narrative and tactical adventure taking place at a time when piracy was at its peak. Here, you can learn more about Savage Level, the studio behind this unique game!

[h2]The studio’s origins: a story of two brothers[/h2]

First and foremost, Savage Level is a family story. Its founders – Aurélien and Maxime Josse – are brothers. As early as the 2010s, they worked together at Tindalos Interactive, the first studio co-created by Aurélien, which released games like Aliens Dark Descent and Battlefleet Gothic Armada. One day, the pair decided to embark on a new shared adventure: “[i]We knew that we could work together, and all the stars were aligned,[/i]” Maxime told us. In May 2021, Savage Level was born.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/f0b613528744dfaef33d35de2cf015f837b29e78.png[/img]

And how did the name come about? In Maxime’s words: “[i]We’re both fans of Rage Against The Machine. One day, while driving, I was listening to a song with the lyrics ‘take ’em to the seventh level’. I heard ‘savage level’, and I thought ‘that sounds awesome!’ It’s like a video game level that’s beyond hard. Later, I realized that I’d misheard, but it didn’t matter, because the name is cool.[/i]” The developers decided to set up their studio at an amazing industrial site in the Butte-aux-Cailles neighborhood of Paris, where they began their work.

When it came to choosing a publisher, Savage Level instinctively turned to Microids for two main reasons. “[i]Microids’ plans to extend their publishing line closely matched what we had to offer,[/i]” said Maxime. “[i]What’s more, we’ve been inspired by comic art to tell the story of [/i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[i], and the group Média-Participations, which Microids is part of, is one of the mainstays of the Franco-Belgian comic book scene.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/b6cd3439a3bf3c7669c6dd93a6cef99593262c9d.png[/img]

[h2]A talented team guided by values[/h2]

Today, the studio Savage Level is formed of 25 people, working in various roles ranging from production to 3D modeling and audio. The third brother of the Josse family – Kristen – is also on the team, working in game design. Heading up the studio are Aurélien, a graphics nerd, who takes care of the production side, while Maxime manages the company’s operations. The pair work in perfect synergy. “[i]We’ve built everything together; we have loads of shared references,[/i]” Maxime enthused. “[i]He only needs to say a few words, and I instantly know what he means. Having that kind of relationship saves so much time.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/44ce0fe33fbefa0d03c9bce8b3bc2a7615922c09.png[/img]

The team is built on strong values. In respect of the team itself, the focus is on inclusiveness. Everybody is welcome at Savage Level, whatever their background or beliefs. “[i]For us, it’s all about people,[/i]” stated Maxime. “[i]We founded this studio primarily to enable people to make a living doing something that they love.[/i]” Their values also extend to the players: “[i]We’re not interested in using ploys to get people hooked and spend their money. Our ambition is to create rich worlds that players will enjoy.[/i]”

[i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i] will be the first game developed by Savage Level, which is set for release on 24 October. But that certainly doesn’t mean it’s a title designed by beginners! Savage Level’s team includes people with more than 25 years of experience in the business. “[i]Collectively, we’ve contributed to more than a hundred games in the past, including both indy and triple A titles,[/i]” pointed out Maxime. The team is preparing an exceptional pirate adventure that breaks new ground with its combat mechanics and comic book-style narrative design.

notes.title: 🏴‍☠️ Drawing inspiration from comics for a truly unique narrative 🖼️
notes.content:
A tactical RPG set in the world of 18th-century pirates, [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i] stands out, not least, for its story told using comic-book codes. In this latest article, we explain how and why Savage Level adopted this original narrative style.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/31294018c87444350c539780875b80d3952fc2f3.jpg[/img]
[h2]A comic-book-inspired narrative dimension[/h2]

In [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i], players explore immersive environments created with Unreal Engine 5, and fight in turn-based combat. The twist is that the story unfolds in the style of a comic book! For example, during a dialogue, a first box appears with our hero and his speech bubble, followed by a second with his interlocutor... In this way, we gradually build up a real on-screen comic strip.

Aside from dialogues, [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i] also uses comic-book codes to accentuate actions and emotions. During a thunderstorm, for example, you'll have the chance to admire a beautiful illustration of a bolt of lightning accompanied by the onomatopoeia "Kraakk!" An image of a surprised face will also pop up when our crew attacks an adversary. Finally, comic bubbles will be integrated into the scenery, above characters’ heads, to share their day-to-day discussions.

Aurélien Josse, Chief Creative Officer at Savage Level, explains the reasons behind this choice: "[i]It all started with the observation that in many narrative games, the story and dialogues are conveyed by large blocks of text, which can be tedious and cause players to lose interest. In seeking a solution to this, I made the link with comics, which have always fascinated me. With their images and pace, they're a much more engaging alternative. And thanks to the comic strip format, it's also possible to display a variety of emotions, which 3D characters can struggle to achieve without the benefit of an AAA budget.[/i]"

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/b883929cad1aa92f28003d2df197f43ca1bf4151.png[/img]
[h2]A first-class team and a complex creative process[/h2]

For Aurélien, this approach is also a way of paying tribute to Franco-Belgian comics, whose reading experience is "a pleasure in itself ". Indeed, Savage Level called on some of the best in the field to produce the artwork for Flint: Treasure of Oblivion! In charge of the drawings is Fabrice Druet, whose work includes Methraton, the spin-off from the Black Moon Chronicles. But also Bruno Tatti, a talented colorist who worked on XIII and Blake and Mortimer…

The team also includes a storyboard artist and several writers. Not forgetting the game designers, who created the comic book system from scratch using Unreal Engine 5. "[i]We had to develop speech bubbles that would adapt to the space taken up by each language, while respecting the layout of the boxes,[/i]" says Aurélien. "[i]Another challenge was to strike a balance between what was shown in the comic strip, in 3D, and in simple speech bubbles. It had to be just right, otherwise the narrative flow wouldn't work.[/i]"

A final challenge was to ensure visual consistency between 3D characters and their comic book alter egos. For this, Savage Level has a process that's fairly unique in the video game industry, first creating concept art, then a comic book version, and finally a 3D model. Thanks to all this work, the studio is confident of offering a truly original game formula at the end of the year. "[i]Our comic-book-inspired narrative is the true innovation of the game,[/i]" comments Aurélien, "[i]and we hope it will leave a lasting impression - but the feedback we're getting from players has already convinced us of that.[/i]"

notes.title: 🏴‍☠️ How do the pirate battles play out in Flint ⚔️
notes.content:
In [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i], players follow the adventures of a pirate crew through phases of exploration, comic-style narration and epic clashes. Today, we will look at the ins and outs of the combat system with [b]Johan Spielmann, Game Director at Savage Level[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/3c74847b4c4188d60e6ab0d79a0a7bb20c28c018.jpg[/img]
[h2]Combat mechanics in Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/h2]

In their quest for riches that will take them all the way to Central America, Captain Flint and his companions will need to fend off many enemies. As a tactical RPG, [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i] features turn-based combat with an overhead view. Each crew member can perform [b]two actions on their turn[/b], or sometimes more if they drink a tonic for example.

Among the possible actions, there are [b]movement [/b]and [b]attack [/b]actions. Characters can move a certain number of squares (in [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i], these “squares” are actually [b]hexagons[/b] that offer a greater number of possible combinations). They can also rush at an enemy and knock them over, or trample them if they are already on the ground. They can even [b]interact with objects in their environment[/b], like barrels, which can be rolled into an enemy.

“[i]The environment plays a big role in Flint: Treasure of Oblivion, and being in the right place can make a huge difference[/i],” Johan commented. “[i]Finding a way to descend on an enemy, or take them by surprise, can maximize damage inflicted. On the other hand, the environment can also be used against you; be careful not to fall from a height, or, even worse, into the ocean.[/i]”

In terms of attack actions, the characters can use [b]a diverse range of weapons[/b], each with its own strengths and weaknesses: daggers, swords, spears, pistols, muskets... Players can also use actions to reload a firearm or protect themselves against a subsequent attack. Their degree of success will be determined by dice-throws, ranging from a critical hit to breaking their weapon for the remainder of the battle!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/bb96d429ea7ae457ffc8eb672609269d39170c60.jpg[/img]
[h2]A combat experience that stands out from other tactical games[/h2]

We asked Johan Spielmann why Savage Level opted for a tactical RPG approach with [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i]. “[i]It’s the most natural game mechanic to tell the whole story of a battle[/i]”, the Game Director explained. “[i]With an action-adventure game, we’re in a visceral relationship between a hero and an enemy. This didn’t fit so well with the adventure of our pirate crew, which stays together until death.[/i]”

In the making of this title, the studio was of course influenced by big names like [i]X-COM[/i] and [i]Final Fantasy Tactics[/i], but it stands out by offering its own take. “[i]First, what makes our combat system special is that the battles are always an extension of the story[/i],” Johan said. “[i]There are no gratuitous battles; they are always woven into the narrative. Next, because we want players to move forward through the story, we made sure the gameplay is intuitive – there’s nothing complex about it. We offer a very simple choice: attack or move. Behind that, however, there’s a lot of depth in terms of the actions as we’ve seen. Our game really embodies the famous maxim 'easy to learn; difficult to master'.[/i]”

The combat sequences in [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i] are designed for those who are familiar with video game rules, without having to be masters of the tactical RPG genre. It is for players who, above all, want to follow and take part in a [b]fantastic pirate adventure around the world[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/510709f94d2357d92bfcdda0dc6753007301040f.jpg[/img]

notes.title: ☠️ What challenge awaits you as a pirate captain in Flint: Treasure of Oblivion?
notes.content:
This year, players will be able to dive into [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i], an all-new tactical RPG designed by Savage Level and published by Microids.

Here, we tell you about the location, the period and the goal of this epic pirate adventure!

[h2]Where and when does [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i] take place?[/h2]
To learn about the historical and geographical setting of Flint: Treasure of Oblivion, we reached out to Savage Level.

Maxime Josse, the French studio’s CEO sets the scene: “[i]The game takes place in 1715. These were tough times for the people, who faced widespread disease and insecurity. At the same time, the world’s great powers were at war, fighting over the Caribbean among other places. For the pirates on the fringes, this was a golden age! They bowed to no governments and made their own laws. At sea, life was even tougher, but there was also plenty of comradeship and solidarity.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/ce2407208d716dd40260abb952bc7dcfbc70254b.png[/img]
Immersing themselves in this fascinating period, players will set sail for several destinations, such as the French town of Saint-Malo, the Caribbean islands, and the deep jungles of Central America.

“[i]We wanted to create a world that’s as authentic as possible[/i],” the creative director, Aurélien Josse, told us, “[i]because, like many players out there, we are fans of the pirate world. So we studied maps of Saint-Malo during this period, and went to the Caribbean to take photographs. We read lots of encyclopedias and historical novels, and spoke with researches specialized in piracy.[/i]”

Savage Level’s aim is to immerse you in a believable eighteenth-century environment, with its buildings, clothing and everyday life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/8e6377212dc177d8bbaeb1e23b88318edb604e72.png[/img]
[h2]Who is the main character and what is his goal?[/h2]
Now you have an idea of the setting for your adventure in [i]Flint: Treasure of Oblivion[/i]; but who will you play as, and what will you set out to accomplish in this tactical RPG? Aurélien revealed that “[i]players will step into the boots of James Flint, an English pirate from the novel Treasure Island. Here, we explore his past, his youth. As shown in the first trailer, Captain Flint begins his adventure stranded at sea after his ship has been sunk. A warship picks him up however and takes him to Saint-Malo. This is where our hero will learn of the existence of a huge treasure trove, beyond imagination.[/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/f59bff3c043dbddee9c7b9d4b913d32bddf318b2.png[/img]
For Flint, the call of adventure and riches is irresistible. So he leaves Saint-Malo – where there is a bounty on his head – to recruit a new crew and make his way to the New World.

It will be no easy journey, as the French, English and Spanish armies have all declared war against pirates! What’s more, captains always face difficult choices to make, and mutiny is a constant threat.

“[i]At first, it appears to be nothing more than a treasure hunt... But a whole lot more lies in wait[/i],” Maxime told us. “[i]Firstly, on a personal level, James Flint will learn much about himself as the adventure progresses. But also, as in any good pirate story, there will be elements of the supernatural. We won’t say any more than that; you’ll have to play the game to find out![/i]”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44962209/dbd7848e71d24aca0cd26fdcc89f8bc3be1a13f8.png[/img]
